title: Service classes
summary: A service is a class that holds the state and behavior of a view. A view refers to a service by its instance name: `BasketService` is `basket`. `{basket.count}` reads a field, and `on:click="basket.add()"` calls a method. Fields hold the state of the view. Methods give its behavior. By default, a service is a page singleton (one shared instance for the whole page). Every component that names it shares that one instance. `NeedsAll` creates one service instance for each component instance. It uses the properties of that component. `Lifetime({"value":"prototype"})` also gives other services one instance for each component. `OnStart` runs after injection (the framework gives the service the objects it needs). It also waits until the component is attached to the DOM (the tree of elements on the page). `OnStop` cleans up work that the service owns. A declared `applicationEventPublisher` field and `OnEvent` replace local publish and subscribe code that you would write by hand. A `Needs` field named after a browser resource receives that resource. There is no general framework object on the instance. Ordinary imports and helper functions still work. Constants are static class fields.
